messages:
Carol (CEO): Kicking off the pricing & packaging Q&A thread from today's all-hands. Post any follow-ups about credits, quotas, rate limits, or packaging tiers and we'll answer live.

Sarah (Product): Quick one — will Starter band credits ever roll over month->month? Customers keep asking.

Ashwin (Finance): Short answer: not by default. Credits are promotional and expire at month end unless explicitly converted to committed credits. We're discussing a 30-day grace for transition months.

Mike (Eng): On rate limits: +1 to clarifying how burst buckets work during scheduled deploys. Do we throttle by tokens/sec or concurrent requests?

Sarah (Product): Good point. Product wants predictable behaviour during deploys so apps don't see sudden 429 spikes.

Mike (Eng): Implementation is tokens/sec with a leaky-bucket at the edge and a per-API-key concurrency cap. During global capacity stress we fall back to per-region throttles first.

Sarah (Product): Can that be surfaced in the Console? Customers want to know the exact numbers for each tier (Starter / Pro / Enterprise).

Ashwin (Finance): We can publish nominal caps per tier (e.g., Starter: 100 req/min, 50k tokens/min; Pro: 1k req/min, 500k tokens/min) but with the caveat: contractual Enterprise SLOs override and Dedicated customers get configurable caps.

Carol (CEO): To be clear: those published numbers are defaults for hosted plans. Dedicated/private customers work with Solutions to pin exact limits.

Mike (Eng): Also heads-up — during sustained high-throughput we enable adaptive batching which changes unit-cost dynamics. If you're testing, try longer sequences and watch the Console throughput graph.

Sarah (Product): Action item: product will draft a short FAQ covering credits expiry, a sample rate-limit table, and recommended fallbacks (client-side backoff + retry-after).

Ashwin (Finance): FYI on credits: we're piloting a small program to allow converting promo credits to 1-month trial credits for qualifying customers. Will share criteria this week.

Mike (Eng): Technical note for SREs & SDK teams: include these headers in responses so clients can be graceful: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `Retry-After`. Example: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 500
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 12
```

Sarah (Product): Nice. Also add a line that streaming responses can be interrupted when concurrency caps are hit — we'll mark that in the docs.

Carol (CEO): Thanks all. If leadership to follow: we'll keep pricing predictable and surface those defaults publicly. Sarah & Ashwin, sync up with Legal on the promo-conversion language. Mike, can you drop a short tech note in eng-docs?

Mike (Eng): Yep, will create an eng-doc & link it from the Console FAQ.

OpsBot: Deployed docs/console-rate-limits v1.0 to staging at 1793457000 :rocket:

Ashwin (Finance): Posting planned copy for the promo conversion pilot in #marketing later today — comments welcome.

Sarah (Product): Thanks everyone. If folks have customer examples that motivated these Qs, DM me and I'll fold them into the FAQ. :thumbsup:
